items.t: The seed of the woman
items.n: The first promise: the woman's offspring will crush the serpent's head. The Vulgate reads 'she shall crush'; the Hebrew 'he'. Paul: 'God sent his Son, made of a woman'.

items.t: In thy seed all nations blessed
items.n: Paul argues from the singular 'seed' — one offspring, Christ — that Abraham's blessing reaches the Gentiles.

items.t: The sceptre shall not depart from Juda
items.n: 'Till he come that is to be sent' (Vulgate). The Lion of the tribe of Juda opens the sealed book.

items.t: A prophet like Moses
items.n: Peter in the Temple: Moses' promised prophet is Jesus.

items.t: The Passover lamb, no bone broken
items.n: The soldiers do not break Jesus' legs; John sees the Passover law fulfilled.

items.t: The bronze serpent lifted up
items.n: 'As Moses lifted up the serpent in the desert, so must the Son of man be lifted up.'

items.t: A son of David enthroned for ever
items.n: Gabriel to Mary: 'the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of David his father... and of his kingdom there shall be no end'.

items.t: Thou art my son
items.n: The coronation psalm applied to Christ at his baptism, transfiguration and resurrection (Acts 13:33).

items.t: Out of the mouth of infants
items.n: Children shouting Hosanna in the Temple; Jesus quotes Psalm 8 to the indignant priests.

items.t: Thou wilt not leave my soul in hell
items.n: Vulgate Psalm 15 (Hebrew 16). Peter at Pentecost: David died and was buried, so he spoke of the resurrection of Christ.

items.t: My God, why hast thou forsaken me
items.n: Vulgate Psalm 21 (Hebrew 22), prayed from the cross.

items.t: They pierced my hands and feet
items.n: The psalm's pierced hands and feet and the dividing of garments; Thomas asks to see the print of the nails.

items.t: They parted my garments
items.n: Lots cast for the seamless tunic — 'that the scripture might be fulfilled'.

items.t: Not a bone shall be broken
items.n: Vulgate Psalm 33 (Hebrew 34): 'the Lord keepeth all their bones'.

items.t: He who ate my bread lifted his heel
items.n: Vulgate Psalm 40 (Hebrew 41), spoken of Judas at the Last Supper.

items.t: Vinegar to drink
items.n: Vulgate Psalm 68 (Hebrew 69): 'in my thirst they gave me vinegar'. 'I thirst' — and the sponge of vinegar.

items.t: Zeal for thy house
items.n: Remembered by the disciples at the cleansing of the Temple.

items.t: The Lord said to my Lord
items.n: Vulgate Psalm 109 (Hebrew 110): how can David's son be David's Lord?

items.t: A priest for ever after the order of Melchisedech
items.n: Hebrews builds its theology of Christ's priesthood on this verse and Genesis 14.

items.t: The stone the builders rejected
items.n: Vulgate Psalm 117 (Hebrew 118), quoted by Jesus after the parable of the wicked husbandmen and by Peter before the Sanhedrin (Acts 4:11).

items.t: A virgin shall conceive
items.n: Matthew quotes the Greek 'virgin' (parthenos); Hebrew almah is 'young woman'. Compare the JPS rendering in the reader.

items.t: Galilee of the Gentiles shall see a great light
items.n: Matthew explains why the ministry begins in Galilee, not Jerusalem.

items.t: A child is born to us
items.n: 'Wonderful, Counsellor, God the Mighty... the Prince of Peace' — the Christmas oracle.

items.t: A rod out of the root of Jesse
items.n: Paul: 'there shall be a root of Jesse, and he that shall rise up to rule the Gentiles'.

items.t: He took our infirmities
items.n: Matthew applies the suffering servant's bearing of sickness to Jesus' healings.

items.t: Led as a sheep to the slaughter
items.n: The Ethiopian eunuch asks Philip, 'of whom doth the prophet speak this?' — and Philip preaches Jesus.

items.t: Reckoned with the wicked
items.n: Jesus at the Last Supper: 'this that is written must yet be fulfilled in me: And with the wicked was he reckoned'.

items.t: The voice of one crying in the desert
items.n: All four Gospels apply this to John the Baptist.

items.t: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me
items.n: Read by Jesus in the synagogue at Nazareth: 'This day is fulfilled this scripture in your ears'.

items.t: Bethlehem, out of thee shall come a ruler
items.n: The scribes' answer to Herod's question.

items.t: Out of Egypt I called my son
items.n: Osee spoke of Israel's Exodus; Matthew reads it again of the Holy Family's return.

items.t: Rachel weeping for her children
items.n: Rachel's tomb near Bethlehem; the slaughter of the innocents.

items.t: The new covenant
items.n: The only Old Testament text to speak of a 'new covenant'; Hebrews quotes it entire.

items.t: Thy king cometh riding on an ass
items.n: Palm Sunday staged as fulfilment; John 12:15 too.

items.t: Thirty pieces of silver
items.n: The price of the shepherd, thrown to the potter — Matthew attributes the composite quotation to Jeremias.

items.t: Strike the shepherd, the sheep shall be scattered
items.n: Spoken by Jesus on the way to Gethsemani.

items.t: They shall look on him whom they pierced
items.n: The lance in his side; also Revelation 1:7.

items.t: Elias must come first
items.n: 'Elias is already come, and they knew him not' — John the Baptist.

items.t: My messenger before thy face
items.n: Jesus on John: 'this is he of whom it is written'.

items.t: Three days in the belly of the fish
items.n: 'The sign of Jonas the prophet' — the only sign given to that generation.

items.t: One like the Son of man on the clouds
items.n: Jesus' answer to the high priest, which the court judges blasphemy.

items.t: I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh
items.n: Peter's Pentecost text.

items.t: The just shall live by faith
items.n: Paul's thesis for Romans; also Galatians 3:11 and Hebrews 10:38.

items.t: A clean oblation among the Gentiles
items.n: The early Church read Malachias' worldwide 'clean oblation' as the Eucharist.

items.t: The tent of David rebuilt
items.n: James at the Council of Jerusalem: the Gentiles were foreseen.

items.t: Behold my servant
items.n: Matthew's longest Old Testament quotation, explaining Jesus' quiet withdrawal: 'he shall not contend, nor cry out'.

items.t: Death swallowed up in victory
items.n: Paul's conclusion to the chapter on resurrection.

items.t: A new heaven and a new earth
items.n: Isaias' last vision and the Bible's last vision.
